sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你的二十多岁心理学》，这是一档非常不专业的播客，在这里我们探讨二十多岁时的一些重大变化

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 与过渡，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Ciao.
sentences.zh: Ciao。

sentences.en: Bonjour.
sentences.zh: Bonjour。

sentences.en: How are we all?
sentences.zh: 大家最近都怎么样？

sentences.en: Lockdown week five, baby.
sentences.zh: 封城第五周，宝贝们。

sentences.en: Just had an extension announced this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早上刚宣布延长。

sentences.en: So here we are, thriving.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们就在这儿，顽强生存。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Andrew Barr, keeping us safe as always.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢安德鲁·巴尔，一如既往地保障我们的安全。

sentences.en: But I hope you guys are all doing well, wherever you may be listening, lockdown or not.
sentences.zh: 但我希望你们都过得很好，无论你们是在哪里收听，不管有没有封城。

sentences.en: Hope the sun is shining, that you're being COVID safe, obviously,
sentences.zh: 希望阳光灿烂，你们注意防疫，当然，

sentences.en: and that something amazing has happened to you this week.
sentences.zh: 并且希望这周有什么了不起的事情发生在你们身上。

sentences.en: I'm just going to jump right into it.
sentences.zh: 我这就直接切入正题。

sentences.en: This topic, the friendship breakup, has been on my mind, haunting my dreams quite a bit for the past month or so.
sentences.zh: 这个话题——友谊的破裂，在过去的一个月里一直盘旋在我的脑海中，甚至有点萦绕在我的梦里。

sentences.en: But I haven't really been able to work up the courage to record it or research it, I think for a few reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我一直没能鼓起勇气去录制它或研究它，我想原因有几个。

sentences.en: Firstly, it's insanely personal.
sentences.zh: 首先，这极其私人。

sentences.en: And although I've talked about, you know, things like unrequited love and hookups and heartbreak on this podcast,
sentences.zh: 尽管在这个播客里我谈论过，你知道的，比如单恋、一夜情和心碎这些事，

sentences.en: this is the first episode where it would just be entirely natural for me to come off looking like the bad guy, which my ego obviously wasn't too fond of.
sentences.zh: 但这是第一期节目，如果我表现得像个坏人，那将是极其自然的，我的小本本（自我）显然不太喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And secondly, I didn't really want to do any injustice or harm to anyone who I was once friends with, who I have, quote unquote, broken up with,
sentences.zh: 其次，我真的不想对任何我曾经的朋友造成任何不公或伤害，那些我“所谓”已经断交的朋友，

sentences.en: which we'll kind of discuss later on.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讨论这一点。

sentences.en: And I think like another reason I was kind of hesitant about recording this is it's kind of painful to look back at experiences like that.
sentences.zh: 我想我犹豫要不要录制这一期的另一个原因是，回首这样的经历有点痛苦。

sentences.en: And I just don't think I was really in the right headspace to like dig deep into past friendships, which were insanely meaningful for me, but which have now faded, fizzled.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得自己当时的心态并不适合去深究那些对我意义非凡、但现在已经消逝、淡去的过往友谊。

sentences.en: And we've gone our separate ways.
sentences.zh: 我们已经分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: But yeah, I've made peace with all those things.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，我已经和所有这些事情达成和解了。

sentences.en: I talked to my therapist about it.
sentences.zh: 我和我的心理医生聊过这件事。

sentences.en: Shout out, Josie.
sentences.zh: 向乔西致敬。

sentences.en: God, I love her so much.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我太爱她了。

sentences.en: You're the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你最棒了。

sentences.en: And she said it was a good idea, perhaps even a little bit healing.
sentences.zh: 她说这是个好主意，甚至可能还有一点治愈的效果。

sentences.en: If I came at it with a wise mind, which is her favorite term.
sentences.zh: 如果我能带着她最喜欢的那个词——理智的头脑来对待的话。

sentences.en: So here we are recording in my car yet again, ready to bury some hatches, discuss the psychology behind friendship breakups and the fizzle.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们又一次在车里录音了，准备放下过去，探讨友谊破裂和渐行渐远的心理学，

sentences.en: And why that age old saying is true.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么那句老话是对的。

sentences.en: You know, if you're not losing friends, you're not growing up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你没有失去朋友，说明你没有长大。

sentences.en: So strap in for a great episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，系好安全带，准备迎接精彩的一期节目吧。

sentences.en: I do just want to say before we get into it, this is not some like personal rant about people who have left my life.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，我只想说，这并不是针对那些离开我生活的人的个人抱怨。

sentences.en: No bad feelings will be shared here.
sentences.zh: 这里不会有任何负面情绪的分享。

sentences.en: I just think it's a really interesting topic.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这是一个非常有趣的话题。

sentences.en: And researching this has caused me to reflect on some of my own friendship breakups.
sentences.zh: 研究这个课题让我反思了自己的一些友谊破裂经历。

sentences.en: And I think throughout this episode, I was particularly reflecting on three friendships in particular that have all ended in the past year.
sentences.zh: 我想在这一整集里，我特别反思了在过去一年中结束的三段友谊。

sentences.en: And I just thought there was heaps to learn in this often, I think, uncharted terrain.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得在这片通常被认为是未知的领域里，有很多东西值得去学习。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think I just received a lot of personal closure looking back at some of those friendships,
sentences.zh: 而且我想回看其中一些友谊时，我确实获得了许多个人的释怀，

sentences.en: thinking about what I could have done differently or maybe what I didn't need to do.
sentences.zh: 思考我本可以做哪些不同的事情，或者也许我根本不需要做的事。

sentences.en: You know, yeah, I'll explain kind of my thinking behind it a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，是的，我稍后会解释一下我背后的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And like I said, a lot of personal closure that I would just love to share.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，有很多个人的释怀，我很乐意与大家分享。

sentences.en: So in researching this episode, I read an article that had probably one of the best titles.
sentences.zh: 所以在研究这期节目时，我读到了一篇文章，它的标题可能是最棒的之一。

sentences.en: And it really, I think, inspired how where I kind of took this episode, the form that it took.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它确实启发了我的这期节目的方向和呈现的形式。

sentences.en: So if you want to read it, its title was Friendship Breakups, The Most Untold Love Story.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想读一读，它的标题是《友谊破裂，最不为人知的情爱故事》。

sentences.en: And isn't that the truth?
sentences.zh: 难道事实不是这样吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that just a big cup of truth?
sentences.zh: 难道这不正是满满的真相吗？

sentences.en: Friendship Breakups or Fizzles, they're just as serious and can create the same feelings and reactions as normal breakups.
sentences.zh: 友谊的破裂或渐行渐远，它们同样严肃，并且会产生与普通分手相同的感受和反应。

sentences.en: You know, the loneliness, guilt, anger, awkwardness, the grief.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，孤独、内疚、愤怒、尴尬、悲伤。

sentences.en: Like grief can be a huge component that I think is often underappreciated and not really too often spoken about.
sentences.zh: 比如悲伤可能会是一个巨大的组成部分，我认为这往往被低估了，而且并不常被拿出来讨论。

sentences.en: And I think friendships also contain just as much love as romantic relationships can and appreciation as well, if you do them right, of course.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你经营得当的话，友谊中蕴含的爱和感激其实并不亚于浪漫关系。

sentences.en: And heaps of studies have proven time and time again that friendships are one of the most important ways to enrich your life.
sentences.zh: 无数的研究一次又一次地证明，友谊是丰富你生活最重要的途径之一。

sentences.en: They improve your well-being.
sentences.zh: 它们能改善你的幸福感。

sentences.en: They aid in the stable release of dopamine and serotonin.
sentences.zh: 它们有助于多巴胺和血清素的稳定释放。

sentences.en: And they can help you, you know, cope with trauma, cope with things like your parents are.
sentences.zh: 它们还能帮你，你知道的，应对创伤，应对像父母那样的事情。

sentences.en: Like friendships are just as important as a part of your social network, as a relationship is.
sentences.zh: 就像友谊作为你社交网络的一部分一样，和恋爱关系一样重要。

sentences.en: So I think that, yeah, they're just as important, but they aren't always held to the same esteem.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，是的，它们同样重要，但它们并不总是受到同等的重视。

sentences.en: And I think this all has to do with how our society creates like an internal hierarchy within our minds of which relationships are more important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一切都与我们社会如何在内心建立一种内部等级制度有关，即哪种关系更重要。

sentences.en: And thus the level of emotions we're able to feel in those relationships and in response to them.
sentences.zh: 从而决定了我们在这些关系中以及针对这些关系所能感受到的情感程度。

sentences.en: So bear with me here.
sentences.zh: 所以请听我解释。

sentences.en: But in this hierarchy, friendships are not given nearly as much importance, I think, as familial or intimate relationships.
sentences.zh: 但在这种等级制度中，友谊显然没有被赋予像家庭或亲密关系那样同等重要的地位。

sentences.en: So, you know, friends are just seen as more plentiful and replaceable, which I think is entirely incorrect.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，朋友只是被视为更多、更容易被取代的，我认为这完全是不对的。

sentences.en: You know, good friendships, stable friendships and lasting friendships are incredibly, incredibly
sentences.zh: 你知道的，好的友谊、稳定的友谊和长久的友谊是极其、极其

sentences.en: rare, but we have been conditioned to place more emphasis on finding and keeping intimate partners.
sentences.zh: 罕见的，但我们已经被植入了一种观念，即把更多的重点放在寻找和维系亲密伴侣上。

sentences.en: And there's a greater expectation of suffering and grief when romantic relationships end,
sentences.zh: 当浪漫关系结束时，人们对痛苦和悲伤有更高的期望，

sentences.en: whereas that kind of reaction over friendships, I don't think is as normalized or expected, which
sentences.zh: 而对于友谊结束时的这种反应，我认为并没有得到那么多的正常化或期待，

sentences.en: is a huge problem as to why we don't really talk about what it kind of feels like to go through a painful end with a friend.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的问题，导致我们并不怎么讨论经历与朋友痛苦的结局究竟是什么感觉。

sentences.en: I think people often underestimate what a big deal it is for a friendship to end.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们常常低估了友谊的结束是一件多么大事。

sentences.en: And they can just be, you know, these breakups of sorts can be just as uncomfortable and sad as romantic endings.
sentences.zh: 而且它们，你知道的，这种分手的确可以像浪漫关系的结束一样让人感到不适和悲伤。

sentences.en: You know, I kind of, I don't really want to stress this point, but I just think it's so important.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有点，我其实不想过分强调这一点，但我只是觉得它太重要了。

sentences.en: Like you can share a similar level of intimacy, memories, vulnerability with someone you were never romantic or sexual with.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以和从未有过恋爱或性关系的人分享相似程度的亲密感、回忆和脆弱感。

sentences.en: And when those relationships come to an end, there is an emptiness in their place because no one is entirely replaceable.
sentences.zh: 而当这些关系走到尽头时，它们的位置就会留下一片空虚，因为没有人是完全可替代的。

sentences.en: And every individual brings something entirely different to your life, even if that friendship is no longer fruitful or successful.
sentences.zh: 每个个体都会为你的生活带来完全不同的东西，即使这段友谊不再硕果累累或走向成功。

sentences.en: I had this actually with someone, like thinking of them, I had this with someone at the end of last year.
sentences.zh: 我去年年底其实就经历过这样的事，想到某个人，我去年年底就经历过。

sentences.en: Um, and I think as much as it was important to no longer speak to this friend and essentially
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为尽管不再和这位朋友说话并且基本上

sentences.en: cut them off, there are times that I really miss them and I miss their presence because we did share a lot of memories and a lot of personal vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 和他们断绝联系是很重要的，但有时候我真的很想念他们，想念他们的存在，因为我们确实分享了许多回忆和许多个人脆弱的时刻。

sentences.en: So it was a hard conundrum and I, and I have had quite a few moments, I won't lie, where
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个艰难的难题，而且我不瞒你讲，我有过好几次这样的时刻，

sentences.en: I've wanted to reach out, where I've wanted to message them, rekindle the conversation, talk kind of about what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想去联系他们，我想给他们发信息，重新燃起对话，谈谈到底哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: Um, but I just realized that it is for the best that we're no longer in each other's lives.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我只是意识到我们不再出现在彼此的生活中才是最好的选择。

sentences.en: And as far as I can see, they're really happy and so am I.
sentences.zh: 而且据我所知，他们过得很开心，我也是。

sentences.en: So I think it's just best to leave it be.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得还是顺其自然为好。

sentences.en: Um, even though it's really fucking awkward when I run into them in dicks and woolies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尽管在百货公司或超市（dicks and woolies）偶遇他们时真的很他妈的尴尬。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, maybe if they're listening to this, they'll know it's about them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，也许如果他们在听这个，他们会知道这是在说他们。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think no one's entirely replaceable, even when you do know that those friendships aren't meant to laSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我认为没有人是完全可替代的，即使你确实知道那些友谊并不注定长久。

sentences.en: Um, and like I said, as important as friendships are, romantic relationships tend to get all the glory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且就像我说的，尽管友谊很重要，但浪漫关系往往占尽了所有的风头。

sentences.en: Um, meanwhile, the platonic ones, they're really undervalued, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与此同时，柏拉图式的友谊，我认为它们真的被低估了。

sentences.en: And I read an excellent chapter of this book.
sentences.zh: 我读过这本书里极其精彩的一个章节。

sentences.en: It's called The Friendship Fix.
sentences.zh: 它叫《友谊修复》。

sentences.en: We definitely recommend it if you're into this kind of literature.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这类文学作品，我们绝对推荐它。

sentences.en: And it's written by this psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 它是一位心理学家写的。

sentences.en: Her name is Dr. Andrea Bonnard.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫安德烈·波纳德博士（Dr. Andrea Bonnard）。

sentences.en: And, um, this is what she kind of explains.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，这就是她所解释的。

sentences.en: Because there is not the weighty expectation of monogamy, which is often associated with romantic relationships, people have a much harder time ending friendships.
sentences.zh: 因为没有通常与恋爱关系相关的沉重的一夫一妻制期望，人们在结束友谊时要艰难得多。

sentences.en: So this was a bit confusing when I first read it.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚读到这里时有点困惑。

sentences.en: And I did think it was like a bit of a stretch, but this is how she explains it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至觉得这有点牵强，但这就是她的解释。

sentences.en: And it makes a lot more sense when you read more of the book.
sentences.zh: 当你读完这本书的更多内容时，它就会变得更有意义。

sentences.en: So when you're in a relationship with someone and you're in a monogamous relationship, a closed relationship, you have to break up with a partner in order to move on to someone
sentences.zh: 所以当你和某人谈恋爱，并且身处一夫一妻制的恋爱关系、封闭式关系中时，你必须和伴侣分手才能继续前进，去寻找

sentences.en: new.
sentences.zh: 新的人。

sentences.en: So you, you know, you have to break up with them.
sentences.zh: 所以你，你知道的，你必须和他们分手。

sentences.en: It's an action that has to happen for you to move on to a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是一个为了让你进入新恋情而必须发生的动作。

sentences.en: But in terms of a friendship, there is absolutely nothing stopping you from avoiding a friendship breakup indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 但在友谊方面，绝对没有任何东西能阻止你无限期地回避友谊的破裂。

sentences.en: Putting off the confrontation and just hanging out with other people instead.
sentences.zh: 拖延对抗，转而去和别的人一起玩。

sentences.en: You know, you can't cheat on your friends the way that you could cheat on a partner.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不可能像背叛伴侣那样背叛你的朋友。

sentences.en: Um, and you can have multiple friends, whereas in relationships, we have that expectation of monogamy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以有很多朋友，而在恋爱关系中，我们有那种一夫一妻制的期望。

sentences.en: Um, so often what happens is we end up staying in these friendships and prolonging them with, you know, little snippets of interactions when we should just be cutting ties.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以经常发生的情况是，我们最终留在了这些友谊中，并通过，你知道的，零星的互动来延长它们，而我们本该一刀两断。

sentences.en: I think also, unlike our romantic relationships or, you know, however, unlike our romantic relationships, um, in which there is kind of an understanding that things may not work
sentences.zh: 我也认为，与我们的浪漫关系不同，或者说，无论如何，与我们的浪漫关系不同，嗯，其中有一种理解，即事情可能不会成功。

sentences.en: out.
sentences.zh: 而这正是你们双方同意的协议的一部分，你知道的，在你的青少年时期或，你知道的，在你的二十多岁时，恋情破裂是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And that's kind of part of the agreement you both sign up for, you know, the inevitability of a breakup from a relationship in your teenage years or, you know, in your twenties.
sentences.zh: 这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: It's an, it's understood.
sentences.zh: 这是浪漫依恋的一种动态，但对于友谊，我们假设我们的朋友会永远存在。

sentences.en: It's a dynamic of a romantic attachment, but with friendships, we assume that our friends will be around forever.
sentences.zh: 我们期望我们会，你知道的，一起老去退休，参加彼此的婚礼，

sentences.en: We expect that we'll be, you know, old people retiring together, meet each other's weddings,
sentences.zh: 见对方的家人，见对方的孩子。

sentences.en: meet the family, meet each other's kids.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果有破裂，我们不仅在为当前失去那个朋友而悲伤，也是在为我们在想象的未来中失去那个朋友而悲伤。

sentences.en: So this means that if there is a breakup, we aren't just grieving the present loss of that friend, but also the loss of that friend in our imagined future.
sentences.zh: 这也使得友谊的结束变得相当尴尬，并且显得没有必要。

sentences.en: It also makes ending of friendships quite awkward and appears unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为什么我们需要和一个朋友分手？

sentences.en: You know, why do we need to break up with a friend?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接让它慢慢淡去，让尘埃落定呢？

sentences.en: Why not just let it fizzle and let the debris settle?
sentences.zh: 我想有时这真的不是一个健康的选项。

sentences.en: I think sometimes that's just not really a healthy option.
sentences.zh: 有时这真的不是一个健康的选项。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's also not the best way to avoid hurt.
sentences.zh: 有时这也是避免受到伤害的不二之法。

sentences.en: Like the last taste of your friendship should not be one of bitterness and resentment.
sentences.zh: 就像友谊的最后一页，不该充满苦涩和怨恨。

sentences.en: So sometimes you do need to have that chat with them.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，你确实需要跟对方好好聊聊。

sentences.en: You do need to talk to them and be like, this isn't really working.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要找他们谈谈，告诉他们这样真的行不通。

sentences.en: The same book I was reading kind of goes into this a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我正在读的那本书里也稍微深入探讨了这一点。

sentences.en: And it concluded that there were two main reasons why friendships end.
sentences.zh: 它总结出友谊走向终结的两个主要原因。

sentences.en: But I think I've added a third because I think it also deserves acknowledgement.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得我得加上第三个，因为这也同样值得我们去认识到。

sentences.en: That's the fizzle.
sentences.zh: 那就是淡出。

sentences.en: So these are the three reasons, the three big fat reasons why this psychologist believes that friendships end.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是三点原因，这位心理学家认为友谊会破裂的三个核心重大原因。

sentences.en: So number one, something bad happens.
sentences.zh: 所以第一点，发生了不好的事情。

sentences.en: A betrayal, circumstances that make you realize that you and that other person can no longer be friends.
sentences.zh: 一种背叛，或是某些处境让你意识到你和那个人再也无法做朋友了。

sentences.en: These are relationships that end because of something really terrible, often resulting in maybe a big fight or something of that genre.
sentences.zh: 这些关系是因为某些极其糟糕的事情而结束的，通常可能会引发一场大吵或诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: It's not repairable.
sentences.zh: 这已经无法修复了。

sentences.en: The fizzle.
sentences.zh: 淡出。

sentences.en: You just lose your chemistry with someone.
sentences.zh: 你只是和某人失去了那种默契。

sentences.en: You drift.
sentences.zh: 你们渐行渐远。

sentences.en: That's that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: No harm.
sentences.zh: 没有伤害。

sentences.en: No foul.
sentences.zh: 没有恶意。

sentences.en: No falling out.
sentences.zh: 也没有闹翻。

sentences.en: You have those friends you were really close to at some point.
sentences.zh: 你总会有那么几个曾经非常要好的朋友。

sentences.en: And now the conversation no longer flows in the same manner.
sentences.zh: 而现在，谈话再也没有了从前那种流畅感。

sentences.en: And you both kind of recognize that you don't really have that same spark.
sentences.zh: 你们两个也都能隐约感觉到，彼此之间已经没有了那种火花。

sentences.en: And finally, incompatibility and values.
sentences.zh: 最后一点，三观不合。

sentences.en: Perhaps you were really good friends for some time.
sentences.zh: 也许你们曾有一段时间是非常好的朋友。

sentences.en: But as you've grown, your compatibility and values in life have changed.
sentences.zh: 但随着成长，你们的人生契合度与价值观已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: Or maybe your values really never aligned in the first place.
sentences.zh: 或者说，你们的价值观打一开始就从未真正契合过。

sentences.en: And something has made you realize that.
sentences.zh: 只是有什么事让你意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: Or just made you realize that you expect different things from each other as friends.
sentences.zh: 或者只是让你意识到，作为朋友，你们对彼此的期望是不一样的。

sentences.en: And I think, in general, this is the most common reason.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，总的来说，这是最常见的原因。

sentences.en: Friendships typically come to an end because there is a disconnect that one or both of you feel is beyond repair.
sentences.zh: 友谊通常会走到尽头，是因为你们其中一方或双方都觉得这种隔阂已经无法修复。

sentences.en: It's not nasty.
sentences.zh: 这并不是出于恶劣。

sentences.en: It's not a negative thing.
sentences.zh: 也不是什么负面的事。

sentences.en: You're simply going through different life transitions that are going to take you to different places.
sentences.zh: 你们只是正在经历不同的人生阶段，而这些阶段会把你们带往不同的地方。

sentences.en: And there's that age-old wisdom.
sentences.zh: 还有那句流传已久的至理名言。

sentences.en: My friend Lucy, she said this to me the other day.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友露西，前几天就跟我说过这个。

sentences.en: People come into your life for a reason, a season, or a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 人们来到你的生命里，或出于某种原因，或为了某个阶段，或伴随一生。

sentences.en: And that applies to friendships, I think, more than any other kind of relationship.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，比起其他任何类型的人际关系，这句话用在友谊上再合适不过了。

sentences.en: Think about all those people that you know from high school who are still friends with the exact same people.
sentences.zh: 想想你认识的那些高中同学，他们至今依然跟同一批人做着好朋友。

sentences.en: There just has to be, I think, some tension and incompatibility in these situations.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在这种情况下，必然存在着某种张力和不合。

sentences.en: You know, how can you be on the same trajectory as every person in your life that you have ever shared a friendship with?
sentences.zh: 你想想，你怎么可能在你人生中建立过友谊的每一个人身上，都保持着相同的轨迹呢？

sentences.en: People change.
sentences.zh: 人是会变的。

sentences.en: And stagnation is really unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 而停滞不前真的很不健康。

sentences.en: It doesn't allow your brain to move, grow, change.
sentences.zh: 它不会让你的大脑去运转、成长、改变。

sentences.en: And it doesn't give you new experiences or new ways to learn with new people.
sentences.zh: 它也不会带给你新的体验，或是让你通过结识新朋友去学习新的相处方式。

sentences.en: Because if you're keeping all those people that you've always been friends with, there's no room for new people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你一直留着所有那些老朋友，就容不下新的人了。

sentences.en: There's no room for someone else.
sentences.zh: 就再也容不下其他人了。

sentences.en: And that kind of means it's necessary to shed old relationships to grow into your new skin.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，为了蜕变成全新的自己，抛弃旧的人际关系是有必要的。

sentences.en: And like I said, imagine if you were friends with every person that you have ever shared a connection with.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，想象一下，如果你和所有曾经有过交集的人都一直是朋友。

sentences.en: Like, it would be a fucking full-time job and more to stay in contact with all of them, to hear about, you know, provide support to all of them, to have to stay up to date with
sentences.zh: 那简直就像一份全职工作还要超额，得和所有人保持联系，去听取、你知道的，为所有人提供支持，还得随时了解

sentences.en: their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们的生活。

sentences.en: Essentially, I think, although that was a bit of a rant, what I'm trying to kind of communicate is that friendships ending is not only normal, but also a necessary part of growth.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，虽然刚才有点像是在发牢骚，但我想表达的是，友谊的结束不仅很正常，也是成长过程中必不可少的一部分。

sentences.en: And it should be something that we are more honest about.
sentences.zh: 而且对于这件事，我们应该抱有更坦诚的态度。

sentences.en: If you and a person are no longer compatible, you have different priorities, you know, why force it at that stage?
sentences.zh: 如果你和一个人已经不再合拍，彼此有着不同的生活侧重点，你知道的，为什么还要在那个阶段强求呢？

sentences.en: Would it not just be better to give each other the freedom to move on and transform into the
sentences.zh: 与其让双方都去迁就那些如今只代表了过去的自己的人，倒不如给彼此自由，去继续前行并蜕变成

sentences.en: new versions of yourselves, rather than you both kind of having to appease those who are now a reflection of a past you?
sentences.zh: 崭新的自己，难道这样不是更好吗？

sentences.en: I think there is one element of friendship breaks-ups that I do really want to touch on, though, because I'm very, not, I don't want to say, like, I'm a pro-friendship-breakup
sentences.zh: 不过，我觉得友谊破裂中确实有一个要素是我很想聊聊的，因为我非常——倒也不是说我是个拥护

sentences.en: person, but I'm pro-cultivating the right relationships for you.
sentences.zh: 友谊破裂的人，而是我拥护为你自己培养正确的人际关系。

sentences.en: We often hear someone refer to an ex-friend as toxic, or they bring negative energy into their life.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到有人把前朋友称为有毒（toxic），或者说他们会给自己的生活带来负能量。

sentences.en: And I'm sure we've all used that word, or, you know, they're toxic as fuck, or their relationship was, like, so, was, like, really toxic, like, they're a toxic person.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定我们都用过这个词，或者，你知道的，他们简直毒透了，或者这段关系简直，就是，真的太有毒了，就好像他们是个有毒的人一样。

sentences.en: And I kind of have always had a bit of a problem with this, like, do toxic people really exist?
sentences.zh: 而我一直对这种说法有点看法，那就是：这世上真的存在所谓有毒的人吗？

sentences.en: Is this a reason to kind of justify ending a friendship with someone, that they're toxic, they're inherently toxic?
sentences.zh: 这能成为证明我们有理由和某人结束友谊的借口吗？就因为他们有毒、骨子里就有毒？

sentences.en: And I do have a particular opinion about this, obviously, that I don't think is necessarily shared by everyone.
sentences.zh: 显然，我对这一点有我自己的独特看法，我并不认为这种看法一定能得到所有人的认同。

sentences.en: But I really don't think that toxic people as a category exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但我真的不认为作为一种分类会存在什么“有毒的人”。

sentences.en: I don't think that anyone in particular is, you know, just toxic to their core.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得具体哪个人，你知道的，就是彻头彻尾的有毒。

sentences.en: People just have friction with other people, and not with others.
sentences.zh: 人们只是跟某些人有摩擦，而跟其他人没有摩擦罢了。

sentences.en: And that creates negativity, and that toxicity that we associate with someone in particular.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点产生了负能量，以及我们加诸在某个人身上的那种“毒性”。

sentences.en: It's not that person, it's your relationship with them, with that person.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那个人的问题，而是你与他们、与那个人的关系的问题。

sentences.en: Not them.
sentences.zh: 而不是他们本人。

sentences.en: And I think those are some, those things that we can't really confuse.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是某些我们真正不该混为一谈的事情。

sentences.en: And because of your relationship, and because it's not compatible, that's what creates that negativity.
sentences.zh: 正是因为你们的关系，并且因为这种关系并不合拍，才制造出了那种负面情绪。

sentences.en: Like, no one is toxic.
sentences.zh: 总之，没有人是有毒的。

sentences.en: I, like, hate that phrase.
sentences.zh: 我，我简直讨厌这个词。

sentences.en: I don't think that we can claim anyone is toxic.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们可以断言任何人是有毒的。

sentences.en: But with that in mind, I do think there, obviously, is a certain point where friendships do cross boundaries, and become an increasingly negative force on your life.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我确实觉得，在某个特定的节点上，友谊显然会越过界限，并对你的生活变成一种日益增强的负面力量。

sentences.en: And psychological research does say there are certain personality types that do tend to
sentences.zh: 心理学研究确实表明，确实存在某些特定的人格类型，他们往往会与他人产生

sentences.en: conflict with others, meaning that those relationships are more likely to be kind of charged with negativity.
sentences.zh: 冲突，这意味着这些关系更有可能充满负能量。

sentences.en: So these types of people have, like I said, distinct personalities or ways of operating socially, but this doesn't make them entirely toxic or toxic for everyone.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这类人有着鲜明的人格或社交运作方式，但这并不意味着他们就完全是有毒的，或者对所有人都充满毒性。

sentences.en: They just might not be the most compatible with you or with the majority of people.
sentences.zh: 他们可能只是和你或者绝大多数人最合不来罢了。

sentences.en: So according to some of this recent research that I stumbled across, and this was really interesting
sentences.zh: 根据我偶然看到的一些最新研究——这真的很有趣，

sentences.en: because I'd never heard of this concept before, but this research suggests that there are at least four basic types of people that we generally may see as toxic.
sentences.zh: 因为我以前从未听说过这个概念，但这项研究表明，我们通常可能视为“有毒”的人至少有四种基本类型。

sentences.en: So the narcissistic aggressive person, the frenemy, the negative complaining person, and the seductive overly dramatic person.
sentences.zh: 那就是：自恋攻击型、亦敌亦友型（frenemy）、消极抱怨型，以及诱惑且过度抓马型。

sentences.en: Starting off.
sentences.zh: 首先来看第一种。

sentences.en: So the narcissistic aggressive type is often someone who is selfish but still highly charming.
sentences.zh: 自恋攻击型通常是那种自私却极具魅力的人。

sentences.en: So they charm and suck you in and can be rather assertive, but they're also inclined towards possessiveness.
sentences.zh: 他们魅力十足、能把你吸引过去，而且可能相当强势，但他们也倾向于极强的占有欲。

sentences.en: So although the initial stages of the friendship may be very gooey and exciting, pleasant even,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管友谊的初始阶段可能会非常甜蜜热烈、甚至令人愉悦，

sentences.en: there is often a degree of rage or anger when things don't go their own way, an intense outburst almoSt.
sentences.zh: 但当事情不如他们所愿时，往往会伴随着某种程度的狂怒或气愤，几乎会彻底爆发。

sentences.en: When you spend time with people or they might perceive that you're neglecting them.
sentences.zh: 当你把时间花在别人身上，或者他们可能会觉得你忽视了他们的时候。

sentences.en: So the frenemy is the next archetype.
sentences.zh: 接下来是第二种原型：亦敌亦友型（frenemy）。

sentences.en: So they seem like a friend but can often become jealous.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来像个朋友，却往往会心生嫉妒。

sentences.en: Perhaps they're prone to gossip and you feel like you just can't trust them.
sentences.zh: 也许他们喜欢八卦，让你觉得根本无法信任他们。

sentences.en: You might even feel inclined to say that they're, or perhaps say that they're deliberately trying
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能会倾向于这么说，或者觉得他们是在故意

sentences.en: to sabotage your happiness amongst other people in order to kind of bolster their self-worth, self-esteem as well.
sentences.zh: 在你和其他人之间破坏你的幸福，以此来巩固他们自己的自我价值感和自尊心。

sentences.en: And by sabotaging those other relationships, it also increases your reliance on them.
sentences.zh: 而通过破坏那些其他人际关系，这也加深了你对他们的依赖。

sentences.en: So the third archetype.
sentences.zh: 第三种原型。

sentences.en: This is the negative complaining person.
sentences.zh: 这就是消极抱怨型。

sentences.en: And this is someone who never, never appears happy.
sentences.zh: 这种人从来、从来没有开心的时候。

sentences.en: They're never satisfied with your friendship and what you have to give them in any way.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们对你的友谊以及你所能给予的一切都从不满意。

sentences.en: Nothing pleases them.
sentences.zh: 什么都无法取悦他们。

sentences.en: And I had a friend like this and my fucking God, it was exhausting.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过这样一个朋友，天哪，这简直让人筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: Being around, you know, someone who regards their life as terrible and can never take encouragement is exhausting.
sentences.zh: 身处一个认为自己的人生糟糕透顶且永远无法接受鼓励的人身边，简直累极了。

sentences.en: It's so tiring.
sentences.zh: 太让人疲惫了。

sentences.en: It makes you feel depressed.
sentences.zh: 这会让你感到沮丧。

sentences.en: It just, you just feel so hopeless and you want to help them.
sentences.zh: 你会感到极其无助，并且很想去帮助他们。

sentences.en: But it's just, sometimes there's just these people who are just ultimately pessimistic.
sentences.zh: 但有时候，总有这样一些人，他们骨子里就是彻头彻尾的悲观主义者。

sentences.en: And perhaps at first, you know, like other archetypes, they appear really friendly and they're open to adventure.
sentences.zh: 也许一开始，你知道的，就像其他原型一样，他们表现得非常友好，并且乐于接受冒险。

sentences.en: But it can often change into passive aggression, a need to dominate your social life and a pattern
sentences.zh: 但这往往会演变成被动攻击、想要主宰你的社交生活，以及一种极难应对、也极难克服的

sentences.en: of negativity that is really difficult to deal with and it's difficult to overcome.
sentences.zh: 负面模式。

sentences.en: And it's, I think, a big indicator of this type of person, the negative complaining person, is that it's emotionally draining to be around them.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这类人（消极抱怨型）的一个巨大标志就是，跟他们在一起会在情感上把人榨干。

sentences.en: And it's emotionally draining to hear how everyone and everything in life is failing them and going poorly whilst you're there, you know, trying to hold them up, trying to support
sentences.zh: 听到生活中每个人和每件事都在辜负他们、一切都在走下坡路，而在你身边，你知道的，你还在试图支撑他们、试图支持

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 他们，这在情感上实在太消耗人了。

sentences.en: Finally, the seductive, overly dramatic person.
sentences.zh: 最后，是诱惑且过度抓马型。

sentences.en: So these people, they're often the life of the party.
sentences.zh: 这类人往往是派对上的焦点。

sentences.en: They're physically attractive, intelligent, charming, exciting, but they steamroll you.
sentences.zh: 他们外表吸引人、聪明、迷人、充满活力，但他们会把你碾压得体无完肤。

sentences.en: They require all of your attention.
sentences.zh: 他们要求得到你全部的注意力。

sentences.en: This is the type of person or individual who never seems to be listening when you're telling
sentences.zh: 这种类型的人或个体，当你正跟他们倾诉你的问题时，他们似乎从不在听，或者

sentences.en: them your issues or they'll, you know, interrupt and trying to make something funny or about them just cut you off.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们会打断你，试图把事情变得搞笑或者扯到自己身上，直接把你噎回去。

sentences.en: They talk over you and they often require a lot of attention and energy, but almost never seem to come through for you or they never really seem to acknowledge you either.
sentences.zh: 他们说话时压过你，并且经常需要大量的注意力和精力，然而几乎从来没有真正为你付出过，也似乎从来没有真正认可过你。

sentences.en: You're just kind of an accessory for them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，你不过是一种配饰罢了。

sentences.en: They crave attention, but it can leave you as the friend feeling pretty depleted and unworthy, unseen or useless.
sentences.zh: 他们极度渴望关注，但这却会让你这个朋友感到精疲力竭、毫无价值、被忽视或觉得自己毫无用处。

sentences.en: So knowing that there are these types of people out there, I'm sure we can all conjure upon some image of someone who would fit into at least one of these four categories.
sentences.zh: 所以，既然知道了世上有这些类型的人，我敢说我们所有人脑海中都能浮现出某个至少符合这四种分类之一的人的形象。

sentences.en: But then there's the question.
sentences.zh: 但紧接着问题就来了。

sentences.en: We all know someone like this.
sentences.zh: 我们都认识这样的人。

sentences.en: So why do we continue to remain friends with people who treat us poorly or who make us feel unappreciated?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们还要继续和那些对我们不好、或者让我们感到不被欣赏的人做朋友呢？

sentences.en: So one reason why we remain friends with people a lot longer than necessary is fear.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以跟某些人维持友谊的时间远超必要，原因之一就是恐惧。

sentences.en: It's fear of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 对孤独的恐惧。

sentences.en: Humans have a natural drive to avoid loneliness.
sentences.zh: 人类有一种逃避孤独的天然驱动力。

sentences.en: It's built into our DNA.
sentences.zh: 这是刻在我们DNA里的。

sentences.en: So when we feel less socially connected or separated or feel like a member of our extended tribe essentially
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们感到社会连接变弱、被疏离，或者觉得我们拓展部落中的某个成员

sentences.en: is treating us poorly or withdrawing, it creates this visceral knee-jerk reaction emotionally.
sentences.zh: 本质上在虐待我们或疏远我们时，它会在情感上引发一种极具本能的膝跳反应。

sentences.en: And as a tribal species, our brains have adapted to rely on social connections as a means to survive.
sentences.zh: 作为一个部落物种，我们的文明演化出依赖社会连接作为生存手段的大脑机制。

sentences.en: So according to this neuroscientist, his name was John Cacioppo.
sentences.zh: 所以根据这位神经科学家的说法，他的名字叫约翰·卡西奥波（John Cacioppo）。

sentences.en: Cacioppo?
sentences.zh: 卡西奥波？

sentences.en: John Cacioppo?
sentences.zh: 约翰·卡西奥波？

sentences.en: I'll put it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我会把它写在节目简介里。

sentences.en: You can have a look at it if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看的话可以去看一下。

sentences.en: He's made a career out of basically just studying loneliness.
sentences.zh: 他把研究孤独当成了自己的一生事业。

sentences.en: It's a really kind of a sad niche.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个有点悲伤的细分领域。

sentences.en: Um, and in one of his recent papers, he made this point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在他的其中一篇最新论文中，他提出了这样一个观点。

sentences.en: So the absence of social connection triggers the same primal alarm bells as hunger, thirst, and physical pain.
sentences.zh: 社交连接的缺失会触发与饥饿、口渴和身体疼痛相同的原始警报。

sentences.en: So this is what leads us to maintain friendships even when they are incompatible or we no longer feel satisfied,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么我们会维持友谊，哪怕它们并不合拍或者我们不再感到满足，

sentences.en: especially if we feel like we have limited options beyond that friend or group of friends.
sentences.zh: 特别是当我们觉得自己除了那个朋友或那个朋友圈之外，选择非常有限的时候。

sentences.en: Additionally, unhealthy friendships can do enormous damage to your confidence levels without you even realising it.
sentences.zh: 此外，不健康的人际关系会在你甚至没意识到的情况下，对你的自信心造成巨大的破坏。

sentences.en: So the idea of leaving what is comfortable, even if it's not fulfilling and going out to find new friends,
sentences.zh: 因此，离开舒适区的想法——哪怕它并不能带来满足感，还要出去寻找新朋友——

sentences.en: it can be extra terrifying if you already are in a place of depleted self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 如果你本就处于自尊心低落的境地，这可能会显得格外可怕。

sentences.en: This also kind of leads on to another reason why we stay friends with people who might not necessarily be the best fit for our character
sentences.zh: 这也顺理成章地引出了我们继续和那些未必最适合我们性格的人做朋友的另一个原因，

sentences.en: or bring out the best aspects of who we are.
sentences.zh: 或者说无法激发出我们最好一面的人。

sentences.en: We want to feel needed.
sentences.zh: 我们想要感受到自己是被需要的。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to feel like they provide value to the world.
sentences.zh: 每个人都希望觉得自己能为这个世界提供价值。

sentences.en: And if we're there for our friends, if we have friends, it makes us feel like we're valuable.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能在朋友身边，如果我们有朋友，这就会让我们觉得自己是有价值的。

sentences.en: And social connections are also an incredibly meaningful and often understated way in which we feel we have purpose.
sentences.zh: 社交联系也是一种极其有意义且常常被低估的方式，让我们感受到自己的人生价值。

sentences.en: Friendships and social ties, they allow us to situate ourselves in our external world.
sentences.zh: 友谊和社交纽带能让我们在外部世界中找到自己的定位。

sentences.en: And internally, they make us feel secure and supported, especially when our presence is serving a function for someone else.
sentences.zh: 而在内心深处，它们让我们感到安全和有支持，特别是当我们对别人而言有存在价值的时候。

sentences.en: The underlying psychology and the socially tuned nature of our brain can also make it exceptionally difficult to end friendships,
sentences.zh: 人类大脑底层心理学和社交本能的特质，也会让结束一段友谊变得异常艰难，

sentences.en: especially if, like in a breakup, we're concentrating on times when our friendships were positive and warm and glowy and nice.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当我们像经历失恋一样，只专注于那些友谊美好、温暖、闪光且愉快的时光时。

sentences.en: Friendships have a honeymoon phase, just like relationships.
sentences.zh: 友谊也有蜜月期，就像恋爱关系一样。

sentences.en: But I think just like relationships, we also tend to outgrow them.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得就像恋爱一样，我们往往也会逐渐超越它们，不再需要。

sentences.en: Like I said, if you're not losing friends, you're not growing.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，如果你没有失去过朋友，说明你没有成长。

sentences.en: But I think the important thing to remember, and I know it's just like, this isn't like a necessarily very wise thing to say, I just think it's a nice way to end the episode,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得需要记住的重要一点是——我知道这听起来未必是什么至理名言，我只是觉得用它来给这期节目收尾挺好的——

sentences.en: is that friends should be there to support you and to enrich your life.
sentences.zh: 那就是朋友应该支持你，并且丰富你的人生。

sentences.en: And if they're bringing you down, it's probably time to move on.
sentences.zh: 如果他们一直在拖累你，那大概是时候前进了。

sentences.en: If you don't enjoy their company, move on.
sentences.zh: 如果你享受不到和他们在一起的快乐，那就离开吧。

sentences.en: The people you choose to surround yourself with should be great spirits and they should inspire you to be the absolute best you can
sentences.zh: 你选择环绕在身边的人应该充满正能量，他们应该激励你成为最好的自己，

sentences.en: and just create that energy that you yourself want to embody and represent.
sentences.zh: 并且创造出那种你自己也想体现和代表的能量。

sentences.en: I think in our 20s, it's inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在二十多岁的时候，这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: You're going to go through a friendship breakup.
sentences.zh: 你总会经历一次朋友之间的分道扬镳。

sentences.en: But recognising when it is time to move on and handling it with grace is kind of our best option at that point.
sentences.zh: 但认清什么时候该向前看，并且优雅地处理它，可以说是我们当时最好的选择了。

sentences.en: Honestly, I don't know, this is a bit weird, but why not have like a breakup chat about it?
sentences.zh: 说实话，我不知道，这听起来可能有点怪，但为什么不就此进行一次“分手谈话”呢？

sentences.en: I've done it with friends before.
sentences.zh: 我以前和朋友这样做过。

sentences.en: It kind of curbs the awkwardness and obviously that's not an option for everyone.
sentences.zh: 这能在一定程度上减少尴尬，当然这并非对所有人都适用。

sentences.en: If someone's done something really terrible to you, cut them out, you know, vibe so high, you don't need them.
sentences.zh: 如果有人真的对你做了很过分的事，那就直接断绝关系吧，你知道的，能量拉满，你不需要他们。

sentences.en: Sometimes, you know, you're just going to have to have awkward run-ins with ex-friends and just hope that you're both mature enough to like not mention it
sentences.zh: 有时候，你难免会和前朋友尴尬地偶遇，只能祈祷你们俩都足够成熟，假装提都不提，

sentences.en: and just ask how each other have been and move on.
sentences.zh: 只是互相问候一下最近怎么样，然后各走各的路。

sentences.en: Be the bigger person.
sentences.zh: 做个大度的人。

sentences.en: Anyhow, I hope you guys enjoyed this episode.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，希望大家喜欢这期节目。

sentences.en: Like I kind of mentioned, it was incredibly cathartic and it's kind of been building up in my notes archive for a while.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，这真的非常宣泄情绪，而且这些内容在我的备忘录里积攒了一段时间了。

sentences.en: So I just think it's super important to talk about friendship breakups.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为探讨友谊破裂超级重要。

sentences.en: They're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这种事随处可见。

sentences.en: We can all think of someone who we're no longer friends with.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都能想起某个不再联系的朋友。

sentences.en: Maybe we even resent them.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能对他们心存怨恨。

sentences.en: We haven't forgiven them for something.
sentences.zh: 为了某些事，我们至今没有原谅他们。

sentences.en: It feels like that friendship felt like a relationship even.
sentences.zh: 那种友谊感觉甚至就像是一段恋爱关系。

sentences.en: So definitely something I think needs to be talked about more.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一个需要被更多讨论的话题。

sentences.en: So I hope that kind of understanding some of the psychology behind it was interesting.
sentences.zh: 希望了解一些背后的心理学对大家有所启发。

sentences.en: And like I said, like I always say, I guess, remember to subscribe to this podcast if you liked it on wherever you're listening.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我总是这么说，如果你喜欢这个播客，记得在你收听的平台上订阅。

sentences.en: Honestly, I'm sure you can subscribe there unless it's like on the website like my grandparents do it.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我确信你在那儿绝对能订阅，除非你是在官网上听的，就像我爷爷奶奶那样。

sentences.en: And I hope that we're all coping well with lockdown and whatever is going on with your life.
sentences.zh: 希望大家都能好好应对封城以及你生活中正在经历的各种事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Feel free to drop some suggestions as well on Instagram if you've got any ideas about what you want to hear about on the next episode of the show.
sentences.zh: 如果你对下一期节目有什么想听的主题，欢迎随时在 Instagram 上给我们留言提议。

sentences.en: And as always, thanks so much for listening.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下期再见。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去真的很专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对我的 Whoop 智能环疯狂着迷。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，大家伙儿，你们知道我是个极其注重数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢打开 Whoop 应用，看我的睡眠、压力、运动负荷是如何与我的心情、跑步表现以及日常感觉相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit and I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 我绝非什么顶尖运动员，但我确实从中获益匪浅，而且我也真的很喜欢深入了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day to day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going,
sentences.zh: Whoop 还能给我提供这些可操作的个性化洞察，让我变得更有意识，这意味着我能对每天的需求做出更明智的决定，而不是只知道踩着油门一路狂奔，

sentences.en: going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 不停地冲、冲、冲。

sentences.en: New members can try Whoop with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅会员之前，可以免费体验 Whoop 30 天。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of Whoop.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com slash psychology 即可免费试用一个月 Whoop。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人保留着他们所有的旧演唱会门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐的记忆。

sentences.en: It brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回回忆，甚至是气味。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 其他人则收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、海外纸币，或是80年代的复古毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是极其私人的。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它展现了我们是谁，但也记录了我们从何而来。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd, Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在全新播客《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，主持人萨姆·托德（Sam Todd）探索了那些构成我们一部分的回忆、痴迷和微小宝藏。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd, stories want to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed with Sam Todd》，Pandora 倾情呈现的故事。

sentences.zh: 立即在 iHeart 上收听该播客。

sentences.zh: 这是一档 iHeart 播客节目。

sentences.zh: 由真人保证。
